instantiation.worst_case: hello.v1.HelloService/Hello is the service's only method. After this change every request whose `name` is empty or all-whitespace gets `InvalidArgument` (gRPC code 3) instead of `hello `. If any deployed caller sends such a name — today the only caller measured is source_workload=traffic in namespace frontend, spiffe://cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend, 1.77-3.1 rps in cluster e1-dev — then 100% of that caller's calls to the service's only method fail, i.e. a total functional outage of hello as seen by that caller. Containment: the fleet has exactly one cluster (fleet: e1-dev, env=dev); hello is ClusterIP only (exposure query: services hello and hello-canary, both ClusterIP), 1 ready instance, no prod cluster exists, no firing alerts, no human end users behind the measured caller. Blast radius is therefore one internal dev service path, but it is that service's entire function, and the promote workflow carries the same digest onward to any environment added later. Two amplifiers to check: the Argo Rollouts analysis gate only counts Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded, so an InvalidArgument storm would not stop the canary; and the e2e probe sends an all-default (empty) request, so the suite may stay green while every call is rejected.

obligations.establish: Establish whether any deployed caller of hello.v1.HelloService/Hello sends an empty or whitespace-only `name`, and what it does with code 3. The only caller measured is source_workload=traffic / sa frontend in e1-dev; service.yaml authorizes smallStepGiantLeap/frontend for this method. Get the traffic generator's actual manifest/args/image (namespace frontend, cluster e1-dev) and, if a real frontend service exists in the org, its call site, and state whether the name it sends can be empty (unset proto3 string defaults to ""). Do NOT accept as evidence the answer added by this same PR to .paved-agent/discover.yaml (`traffic_generator_sends_blank_names: no`) — that line is authored by the change under review and asserts the review's conclusion; it must be corroborated by the generator's own manifest or source, and if it cannot be, the answer stands unverified.

Unit tests cover both new branches (TestHelloRejectsEmptyName for " ", TestHello for "  Ada "), but the old input "" -> "hello " case was deleted rather than re-asserted, so no test records that the old contract was intentionally broken. Critically, establish whether the platform's e2e suite still proves the service answers: e2e/probe/main.go invokes the method with &emptypb.Empty{} (name=""), so every e2e call now returns InvalidArgument; the `reach` matcher in e2e/run.sh:227 accepts any CODE except PermissionDenied|Unavailable|DeadlineExceeded, and tally()'s `failure` list (probe/main.go:89) excludes InvalidArgument so the drain check's `failed=0` still holds. summary: Verdict: blocking, on correctness. The change is well-tested and load/security/availability-neutral, but the one caller it could break — the dev traffic generator — has no discoverable source in the org, so the self-added discover.yaml claim that it 'never sends blank names' is an unverified assumption authored by this same PR. Separately (warning): the canary analysis ignores InvalidArgument so a total-rejection regression would auto-promote, and the e2e suite's own simulated caller sends an empty name yet both its reach and no-errors checks would still pass green, meaning no automated gate in this pipeline would catch this change being wrong about its one real caller.
